cleaning_logic: The script reads raw.csv with every column as text, strips whitespace from all values and normalises the missing tokens ('', NA, N/A, null, None, '-'; case-insensitive) to missing (R1). It then removes duplicate order_id rows keeping the first occurrence in raw-file order, and drops rows with no order_id since the schema requires it non-null (R2). Each subsequent filter is applied in order with per-rule drop counts: order_date is parsed strictly against the five allowed formats (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/DD/YYYY, DD-Mon-YYYY, YYYY/MM/DD, 'Month D, YYYY') using locale-independent English month tables, validated as a real calendar date, and rewritten as YYYY-MM-DD (R3); region is mapped case-insensitively to North/South/East/West including the N/S/E/W abbreviations (R4); product_category is mapped case-insensitively (with whitespace normalisation) to the five allowed categories including the listed variants Electronic, Home and Garden, Home&Garden, Sport, Apparel, Book (R5); unit_price has '$', 'USD' and ',' removed, is parsed as a number and must be in (0, 5000] (R6); quantity must parse as a whole number in [1, 50] and is stored as int (R7); discount_pct has a trailing '%' removed, missing values become 0, and values must be in [0, 100] (R8); customer_id is upper-cased with missing set to 'UNKNOWN' (R9). Finally revenue = quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct/100) rounded to 2 decimals is added (R10), the nine required columns are emitted in order, sorted by order_id ascending, and written to cleaned.csv without index or currency/percent symbols (R11). cleaning_summary.json records raw_rows, cleaned_rows and per-rule counts (duplicates removed, invalid-date/region/category/price/quantity/discount drops, missing discounts set to 0, missing customer_ids filled).
